h1: Do I need a permit to cut down a tree in Newton, MA?
title: Newton Tree Preservation Ordinance: When You Need a Tree Permit
description: Newton's Tree Preservation Ordinance (Ch. 21): which trees are protected (6 inches DBH and up), when a tree permit is needed, and replacement rules.
short_answer: Often, yes. Trees 6 inches or more in diameter at breast height (measured 4½ feet above grade) on covered land are protected. You need a tree permit before removing a protected tree or starting work under an Exterior Work Permit. Even exempt trees need an exemption permit before removal.

facts.text: Protected trees include trees at least 6 inches DBH on covered land, plus replacement trees (Sec. 21-81).
DBH is measured 4½ feet above grade at the base of the tree (Sec. 21-81).
A tree permit is required before removing a protected, non-exempt tree, or before starting work under an Exterior Work Permit (Sec. 21-82(b)).
Even an exempt tree requires an exemption permit before removal (Sec. 21-82(c)).
Required replacement is due within 18 months of the tree permit, or before the property changes hands, whichever comes first (Sec. 21-85(a)).
Replacement trees must be planted on the same lot (Sec. 21-85(a)(2)).
Applicants may plant replacements, pay in lieu, or combine the two.
Replacement trees are protected and get at least Significant Tree status, whatever their trunk size (Sec. 21-85(a)(5)).

qa.q: What size tree is protected in Newton?
qa.a: Trees at least 6 inches DBH on covered land, measured 4½ feet above grade.

qa.q: Do I need a tree permit for a construction project?
qa.a: A tree permit is required before starting work under an Exterior Work Permit (Sec. 21-82(b)).

qa.q: Can I pay instead of replanting?
qa.a: Yes. The City lists planting, payment in lieu, or a combination.

qa.q: When must replacement trees be planted?
qa.a: Within 18 months of the tree permit, or before the property changes hands, whichever comes first.
